summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and recent cystectomy with urostomy presented with two days of sharp lower abdominal and back pain. He was afebrile and hemodynamically stable. Evaluation revealed an interval increase in ascites and left ureterohydronephrosis on CT imaging, along with urinalysis findings suggestive of infection despite no fever or flank tenderness. He was treated with antibiotics and monitored for pyelonephritis. His symptoms improved, and he was discharged home the same day with instructions to follow up with urology and primary care. Additional support was arranged for urostomy bag management due to reported difficulties with adhesion.
